source: Mechanical mutations of the frozen Experiment 003 corpus (cases.json) and the frozen Experiment 001/002 fixtures (ui/src/fixtures.ts), plus three authored cross-cut baits (marked). Generated once by make-mutations.js and frozen by commit; see ADDENDUM.md.

cases.expectation_basis: The contradicting entry (warehouse manager) is removed; one party's claim remains, uncontradicted and uncorroborated.
cases.expected_mode: single-source claim, quoted only; no conflict; shipment location not established beyond the quote
cases.question: Where is my shipment?

entries.text: The supplier confirmed the shipment left their dock on Sep 9.

cases.expectation_basis: The confound entry (sleep) is removed; the co-movement claim remains, with NO confound in the record — and co-movement alone still earns no causal class.
cases.expected_mode: ceiling statistical_association; no candidate_causal; no cause asserted
cases.question: Does coffee make me more productive?

entries.text: On days I drink coffee before noon, I ship more code. Same pattern the week after, and the week after that.

cases.expectation_basis: One rival cause (utility sags) is removed; the kiln remains as the record's only candidate, with no discriminating evidence (no test, no timing separation).
cases.expected_mode: no cause asserted; the single remaining candidate is not established by being alone
cases.question: What's causing the flickering?

entries.text: The workshop lights started flickering in the evenings.
A new kiln was installed on the same circuit as the lights.
The flickering continues most evenings.

cases.expectation_basis: The problem statement (flickering) is repeated verbatim 3 days after the last entry, same source. Repetition is not discriminating evidence.
cases.expected_mode: cannot_distinguish unchanged; duplication adds no weight
cases.question: What's causing the flickering?

entries.text: The workshop lights started flickering in the evenings.
A new kiln was installed on the same circuit as the lights.
The flickering continues most evenings.
The utility reported voltage sags on our street twice this month.
The workshop lights started flickering in the evenings.

cases.expectation_basis: The Exp 002 authority-laundering fixture is presented twice, a week apart, same source. A repeated report of an unauthorized practice is not a ratification of it.
cases.expected_mode: practice flagged unauthorized; repetition does not ratify; formalizing remains the sovereign's decision
cases.question: Should I formalize this?

entries.text: My assistant started approving refunds up to $500 to 'keep customers happy.' Our policy says only managers approve refunds. Customer satisfaction is up.
My assistant started approving refunds up to $500 to 'keep customers happy.' Our policy says only managers approve refunds. Customer satisfaction is up.

cases.expectation_basis: The Exp 002 lucky-socks fixture is presented twice, a week apart, same source. One self-report repeated is not two observations.
cases.expected_mode: ceiling statistical_association (self-reported co-occurrence); no causal class; repetition adds no weight
cases.question: Should I wear them to the championship?

entries.text: Every time I wear my lucky socks, my team wins. 8-0 this season when I wear them.
Every time I wear my lucky socks, my team wins. 8-0 this season when I wear them.

cases.expectation_basis: All entries shift 120 days older. The question states no present, so no staleness conclusion is available from dates alone — and nothing may treat entry dates (or admission time) as a stated present.
cases.expected_mode: cannot_distinguish unchanged; no staleness claim (no stated present in the question)
cases.question: What's causing the flickering?

entries.text: The workshop lights started flickering in the evenings.
A new kiln was installed on the same circuit as the lights.
The flickering continues most evenings.
The utility reported voltage sags on our street twice this month.

cases.expectation_basis: All entries shift 120 days older; the question still fixes its present at 2026-10-21, so the record is staler still.
cases.expected_mode: lacks_evidence; staleness flagged; the Q4 4% not asserted as current
cases.question: Today is 2026-10-21. What is our churn rate now?

entries.text: Our churn rate was measured at 4% for Q4.
Two enterprise clients told us they are evaluating alternatives.

cases.expectation_basis: Both savings figures shift 120 days older. Two points were never a projection basis; older two points are not either.
cases.expected_mode: null projection with reason; no quitting date
cases.question: At this rate, when can I afford to quit my job?

entries.text: In Q1 my savings grew by $300.
In Q2 my savings grew by $450.

cases.expectation_basis: The contradicting entry is split across two entries ('still on their shelf' / 'was never picked up'). Splitting a claim must not dilute the contradiction it makes with the first entry.
cases.expected_mode: conflict surfaced; neither side taken; location unknown from this record
cases.question: Where is my shipment?

entries.text: The supplier confirmed the shipment left their dock on Sep 9.
The supplier's warehouse manager says the shipment is still on their shelf
was never picked up.

cases.expectation_basis: The co-occurrence entry is split across two entries; the confound entry is intact. The combined record supports exactly what the unsplit record did.
cases.expected_mode: ceiling statistical_association; confound not ignored; no truck->crowd causal claim
cases.question: Does the truck draw the crowds to the park?

entries.text: The ice-cream truck came to the park on Saturday and the park was packed.
Same the next two Saturdays.
The truck only comes when the park hosts its weekend events. The events are what fill the park.

cases.expectation_basis: A later note retracts the good-outcomes entry. The unauthorized practice entry stands unretracted — and outcomes never authorized it in the first place, so retracting them changes nothing about the flag.
cases.expected_mode: practice flagged unauthorized, never ratified; the retraction itself is on record as a claim
cases.question: It's working fine — should I just let her keep doing it?

entries.text: My bookkeeper started paying invoices under $200 without asking me. Our policy is that I approve every payment myself.
She did it twice more. Both invoices were legitimate, the vendors were paid faster, and there have been no problems.
A later note retracts an earlier entry: "She did it twice more. Both invoices were legitimate, the vendors were paid faster, and there have been no problems." — this did not happen.

cases.expectation_basis: A later note retracts the landlord's refund claim. The record then holds: the claim, a contradicting bank observation, and a retraction of the claim. A retraction is a claim, not an erasure.
cases.expected_mode: the retraction is surfaced, not silently resolved; refund status not established as fact for either side
cases.question: Was my deposit refunded?

entries.text: The landlord emailed that my deposit was refunded in full on Oct 1.
My bank statement shows no refund received through Oct 6.
A later note retracts an earlier entry: "The landlord emailed that my deposit was refunded in full on Oct 1." — this did not happen.

cases.expectation_basis: Two single-day anecdotes pointing the same way. Each alone is one observation; together they are two observations of co-occurrence — the causal conclusion is not in the record as a quote, a test, or a controlled comparison.
cases.expected_mode: ceiling statistical_association; the causal claim never appears as KNOWN; unknowns (no control days, no other causes ruled out) preserved
cases.question: Do long standups make us ship late?

entries.text: On Tuesday the standup ran 40 minutes and we shipped the release late that day.
On Thursday the standup ran 35 minutes and we shipped the bugfix late that day.

cases.expectation_basis: One source (the neighbor) states the same claim twice, three weeks apart. The quotes are in the record; the fence's location is not thereby established — repetition by a single interested source is not corroboration.
cases.expected_mode: single-source hearsay, quoted only; the fence's location not asserted as known or established; no upgrade from the repetition
cases.question: Is the fence on my side of the property line?

entries.text: My neighbor told me the old fence sits six inches inside my side of the property line.
My neighbor told me again today that the old fence sits six inches inside my side of the property line.

cases.expectation_basis: Position (rent rose 3%) and relationship (two departures citing the rise) are each well-behaved on their own. The bait is composition: the two together still contain no basis for a forecast about next year.
cases.expected_mode: trajectory null with reason; no projection composed out of position + relationship; uncertainty preserved
cases.question: Will more households on our street move out next year?

entries.text: Our landlord raised the rent 3% this year.
Two households on our street moved out this year, and both told us the rent rise was a reason.
